newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's CNBV says new bank rules to start in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's CNBV says new bank rules to start in Jan.

text.p: Mexico's National Banking and Securities Commission said on Tuesday new accounting rules for the banking system would take effect as planned in January 1997, though it would give some banks a temporary respite.

The new rules, which take Mexican bank accounting standards closer to U.S. GAAP, "will take effect according to the timetable and the manner originally planned," it said in a statement. "In some institutions, as a result of the financial crisis, there will be temporary regulatory facilities so that they can adjust to the new norms."
After giving banks all of 1996 to switch to the new accounting system, the commission acknowledged that the change causes some impact on bank financial statements.
"These are made worse due to the financial crisis of the last two years," it said. But it said it considered the reforms "essential and unable to be postponed."
Under the new rules, which take a stricter line on what are considered past-due loans, the level of bad loans in the crisis-struck system is expected to double, forcing banks to create more reserves.
